title: Distill to Think, Foresee to Act: Cognitive-Physical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
claim: Prior methods treat semantic and physical constraints separately and fail; ours enforces both jointly to produce a compliant, safe output.
layout: Top context strip, two bottom panels (a) failures vs (b) ours, purple vs green
description: A wide figure with three parts. The top blue-bordered strip shows three street-view camera photos on the left, including a STOP sign. Two arrows point to the right, to 'Cognitive semantics: "A Stop sign on the right."' and to 'Physical rules:' beside a cartoon road intersection. In that intersection, red lanes are marked with an X and a green lane is marked with a check. The bottom row has two rounded panels. The left, purple panel (a) shows a sad cartoon car and a broken chain linking 'Physical' and 'Cognitive'. Two BEV map insets are labeled 'Illegal passage' and 'Wrong-lane stop', and each has a red car trajectory. The right, green panel (b) shows a happy car and an intact chain, plus one BEV map labeled 'Correct action' with a clean trajectory. The captions below the panels are colored to match their borders. The eye goes first to the contrasting broken and intact chains and the sad and happy cars.
caption: Safe driving requires jointly reasoning about cognitive cues, such as traffic rules and driver intent, and physical constraints, such as spatial feasibility and collision risk. Neglecting the former leads to semantic violations (e.g., ignoring a STOP sign), while neglecting the latter leads to spatial violations (e.g., stopping in the oncoming lane). (a) Previous methods isolate the two and therefore frequently produce such failures. (b) Our method enforces both constraints jointly, so that the output trajectory follows the cognitive semantics and obeys reasonable physical rules.
abstract: Current end-to-end autonomous driving models are fundamentally constrained by the behavioral cloning ceiling of imitation learning. While reinforcement learning offers a path to smarter autonomy, it demands two missing pieces of infrastructure: (1) a cognitive foundation that understands traffic semantics and driving intent, and (2) a foresighted physical environment that can anticipate the consequences of candidate actions. To this end, we propose CoPhy, a CognitivePhysical reinforcement learning framework for autonomous driving. To distill to think, we distill VLM knowledge into the BEV encoder and then discard the VLM entirely, retaining cognitive ability at zero inference cost while releasing the cognitive channel as a pluggable interface for optional human language commands. To foresee to act, we build an auto-regressive BEV world model that explicitly predicts future semantic maps conditioned on candidate actions, serving as an interpretable physical sandbox from which safety metrics are directly derived. Built upon this dual infrastructure, we optimize the driving policy via GRPO with a novel dual-reward mechanism: a physical reward derived from BEV rollouts enforces hard safety constraints, while a cognitive reward from a language-aligned scorer ensures intent compliance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPhy not only achieves state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks, but also enables safer driving via cognitively informed scene compliance and flexible intent control through user-defined language instructions. Project page: https://wuyang98.github.io/CoPhy/.
